label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 188.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer is stuck on one event it cannot book. It was redeployed at 06:36:30 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. At 06:36:32, evt_000272 (provider-events partition 0, offset 86) arrived with an amount the ledger rejects: 'amount must be positive integer cents'. Under retry, the consumer retries that message forever, with backoff capped at 15 s, and never commits past it. Later events pile up behind it, and lag went from 0 to 234. The money check therefore cannot settle. payment-confirmer (BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter) dead-lettered the same event and moved on. Still open: the ledger's BAD_EVENTS setting before 06:36:30 (likely dead_letter, but unverified); where the bad amount came from (payload not inspected); and why klaxon_dead_letters_total has no series.

evidence.shows: Ledger lag was 0 at 06:35:36 and 06:36:36, then 234 at 06:37:36. A sudden backlog confirms the symptom.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 06:36:30 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry, the only change just before the lag. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.

ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/0@86, attempts 3 through 9 from 06:36:34 to 06:37:33, error 'amount must be positive integer cents', backoff growing to 15 s.
Offset 86 is evt_000272, queued at 06:36:32. payment-confirmer dead-lettered it. ledger-consumer failed it 11 times over 75 s, each with outcome will_retry.
This is the only errored ledger-consumer trace in the last 10 minutes: a single poison event.
klaxon_dead_letters_total has no series even though the trace shows dead-lettering: an observability gap.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before 06:36:30, presumably BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-letters evt_000272 and drains the backlog. Before approving, check in the deploy log what the previous settings were, including LEDGER_HANDLER. Afterwards, inspect evt_000272's amount and the payment or refund it refers to, book it correctly by hand or replay it once fixed, and rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses briefly while its container is recreated, and lag grows slightly. If LEDGER_HANDLER also reverts, booking behavior changes for every event. evt_000272 stays unbooked until repaired, so the money check will flag it. If the previous setting was also retry, the rollback will not unblock anything.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry) as recorded in recent_deploys. Dead-lettered events can be replayed afterwards.
